newsitem.title: DUBAI: GCC chief arrives in Qatar.
newsitem.headline: GCC chief arrives in Qatar.

text.p: The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) arrived in Doha on Saturday as part of regional tour to prepare for the next Gulf Arab summit which diplomats expect to be held in Doha on December 22-24.
The Official Qatar news agency said GCC Secretary-General Jameel Hujilan held discussions with Qatar Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani and other officials.
Hujilan will also visit Oman, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, Riyadh-based GCC officials told Reuters in Dubai by telephone.
The tour comes amid border rows and political differences within the 16-year-old Gulf alliance.
He visited Bahrain on Monday in an apparent attempt to convince the island state's ruler to attend the summit, diplomats said.

Bahrain and Qatar are locked in a territorial dispute over a cluster of barren reefs and islands which are potentially rich in oil and gas. They include Hawar islands, which have been controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.
Bahrain has threatened to boycott the summit in protest against Qatar's failure to withdraw a case it has taken to the International Court of Justice to settle the dispute.
Qatar said it would only withdraw the case from the world court in the Hague if Saudi Arabia's mediation succeeded in settling the long-standing border row.
Qatar asked the court in 1991 to settle the problem. The court decided in January it had jurisdiction and is expected to produce a verdict by the end of this year.
